_note: Positions are the owner's, read out of Highway_19_Website2.svg. The art column is x 288.9 wide 1924.33; anything outside it (the waves) is deliberate bleed.

anchors._why: the owner: the waves should start right after the text

His composition ends with the rocks at the very bottom of his artboard. Pinning that to the top of the first section that is NOT his gives the tail of the scene a real destination instead of extrapolating: without it the rocks are placed at his height times the page scale, which at 3840 is 1685px instead of 842 and runs a long way past the handover.

bands.name: sand
bands._note: Behind everything between the water and the green. Pieces keep their own aspect, so on a page taller than his canvas they fall short of each other; this catches the gap in the right colour instead of the page showing through.

pieces.name: Tree line
pieces._why: His idea: one set of trees repeated horizontally with a 150px overlap, instead of one enormous forest that cannot stretch. Rasterised, not vector - the set is 4,185 shapes, so three across (12,555) would be worse than the 10,112-shape forest it replaces. As an image the browser decodes it once and every repeat after that is free, however wide the screen.

pieces.name: End rocks
pieces._fit: span, not stretch: stretch takes the LARGER of his height and the mapped span, which is the right guard for a band in the middle of the scene that must never leave a gap. This is the closing band and has to meet the handover exactly, at every width, so it takes the span as given.

_signs: Hero Sign and Our sign are deliberately NOT placed here. They are in index.html with real HTML copy over the owner's plate, so the headlines stay selectable and findable rather than being pictures of words.
_z: Paint order inside the scene layer. The sand goes down first and the water's edge cuts over it — the other way round buries his shoreline under the sand.
